killed_findings.dimension: Gate D — memory retention (chance_corrected_recall_ratio >= 0.90 AND feedback_free_return_balanced_accuracy >= 0.70)
killed_findings.title: The ratio is never clipped to [0, 1] and is never flagged when it exceeds 1, so an arm that improves without feedback is scored as having 'retained' memory
killed_findings.refutation: The code fact is true — nothing between line 593 and the gate at 1119-1131 clamps or warns, and I reproduced reference=0.60/return=0.95 → 4.500000000000001, which passes both clauses. But the finding establishes no defect independent of Finding 3. Every false-pass scenario it constructs is driven by a weak denominator, which is Finding 3's defect, not the absence of a clip: with a strong reference, ratio > 1 means the arm matched or beat its own 128-label endpoint with zero feedback after intervening contexts, which is the retention property the gate names, not a false pass. The one piece of real-data evidence cited is wrong: transformer_full_online's raw_recall_ratio of 1.1265 never reaches Gate D at all — its chance_corrected_recall_ratio is None (reference 0.484375 <= 0.5), and raw_recall_ratio is not read by _decision_gates or any other gate. Clipping the ratio to [0,1] would not change a single pass/fail outcome that Finding 3's missing reference floor does not already change.

killed_findings.code:

            and return_accuracy is not None
            and float(recall) >= 0.90
            and float(return_accuracy) >= 0.70

killed_findings.refutation: The load-bearing premise is refuted by direct measurement. The claim 'for any arm whose return-routing is stable the ratio clause is exactly 1.0 and carries zero information' inherits Finding 1's identity, but that identity holds only under ORACLE routing. Under LEARNED routing predict() returns a mixture over all slots (adrn2b_router.py:479) and intervening updates write into non-argmax slots above minimum_responsibility=0.03 (measured: 29/256 intervening steps write >1 slot; phase-0 slots drift 2.31 and 0.72 in adapter norm over phases 1-2). Gate D reads only workspace_meta_learned (line 1104), a LEARNED arm: its ratio is 0.2523, and all 4/4 of its returns differ from their first endpoints (0.53125 vs 0.78125, 0.4802 vs 0.4921, 0.6429 vs 0.7143, 0.46875 vs 0.5). return_accuracy (0.5308) does NOT equal reference_balanced (0.6219), so the gate does not reduce to an acquisition restatement and the ratio clause is not information-free. The only accurate residual — that the gate imposes no floor on the reference, so reference 0.60 / return 0.72 gives ratio 2.2 and passes both clauses (I executed this and got exactly 2.2) — is Finding 3's defect restated.

killed_findings.title: All three evaluators look up the probe set by positional index into an array whose ordering is never validated, and the field that does carry the identity invariant is dead
killed_findings.refutation: The code observations are accurate but they do not constitute a Gate D defect, and one central characterisation is wrong. The lookup `episode.probe_sets[("A","B","C","D").index(phase.slot)]` at lines 380/708/825 is a pure function of phase.slot, so both visits to the same slot NECESSARILY resolve to the identical probe_sets element regardless of ordering — Gate D's stated invariant ('same immutable probes at first endpoint and feedback-free return') is guaranteed by the very line the finding criticises. Moreover that check would not catch the hypothesised failure anyway — I constructed an episode with probe_sets reordered to ('B','A','C','D') via dataclasses.replace and __post_init__ ACCEPTED it, because probe_by_slot is rebuilt from the reordered tuple and the `is` comparisons still hold. The hypothetical failure mode is a target/feature mismatch that would affect every metric in the harness identically, is not specific to retention, and the finding itself verifies it does not obtain today (make_adrn2b_episode builds probe_sets by iterating contexts, whose order IS validated at adrn2b_tasks.py:743).

killed_findings.refutation: The algebra is right but the empirical claim is refuted by instrumenting the actual run. killed_findings.dimension: Gate E — efficiency (ADRN A(32) vs full-online Transformer A(32), and capacity_online_state_bytes)
killed_findings.title: capacity_online_state_bytes uses two different accounting rules: the comparator's frozen backbone counts, ADRN's identical-sized frozen backbone counts as zero
killed_findings.refutation: REFUTED on both the arithmetic and the premise. (a) The number Gate E actually reads is NOT 48,088. adrn2b_experiment.py:519 sets `capacity_online_state_bytes = capacity_bytes + maximum_support_bytes`, and the harness's own output (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cell/0f039315-b3a9-52ac-8187-9fae0d726994/scratchpad/out/adrn2b_smoke.json, decision_gates.E_efficiency.value) reports ADRN_online_capacity_bytes = 1,182,568 versus Transformer_online_capacity_bytes = 270,924. I reproduced the split: 48,088 non-buffer + 1,134,480 meta support buffer. ADRN already LOSES the byte leg by 4.4x and Gate E's passed=False. The finding's counterfactual ('apply the rule symmetrically and ADRN loses') describes an outcome that is already the observed outcome, and its stated advantage (48,088 < 270,924) never exists for the finalist, because `workspace_meta_learned` always carries a meta_initializer and therefore always carries the buffer term. The verdict is decided by the support buffer, not by which frozen parameters get named 'online'. (b) The premise 'two different accounting rules' misreads the metric. It is one rule -- state each deployment must ALLOCATE AND MUTATE -- applied symmetrically. The comparator's backbone is deep-copied fresh per episode (adrn2b_experiment.py:699 sits inside `_evaluate_full_online_episode`), set requires_grad_(True) (adrn2b_models.py:477-478), enrolled in AdamW (485-489) and mutated by every `update` (532-542). ADRN's GRU is explicitly frozen (adrn2b_models.py:446-448 `requires_grad_(False)`) and exists as ONE read-only copy shared across all episodes via the precomputed cache. Counting a fine-tuned per-episode copy and not counting a globally shared frozen one is the definition of the metric, not a naming choice. (c) The harness discloses the frozen backbone for both arms under the identically named key `stable_learned_parameters` (adrn2b_experiment.py:680 for the router arms, 757 for the comparator -- 21,568 vs 21,599 in the artifact), plus `meta_initializer_parameters` for ADRN. Nothing is hidden; Gate E is simply not a total-resident-memory gate.

killed_findings.dimension: Gate E — efficiency (ADRN A(32) vs full-online Transformer A(32), and capacity_online_state_bytes)
killed_findings.title: 'capacity_online_state_bytes' is a capacity bound on one arm and an observed maximum on the other, with a hybrid on the ADRN side
killed_findings.refutation: REFUTED on magnitude -- the discrepancy is provably ~0 on one side and 0.68% on the other, against a figure the two arms differ on by 4.4x. On the comparator side the 'observed maximum' is exactly the architectural capacity, not a loose observation: AdamW allocates exp_avg and exp_avg_sq for every parameter on the first step, so `maximum_optimizer_scalars` saturates immediately. I verified from the artifact: optimizer_state_scalars = 45,154 = 2 x online_mutable_parameters (22,577) exactly, and 4*(22577+45154) = 270,924 = the reported figure to the byte. There is no bound-vs-observation gap on the comparator at all. On the ADRN side the gap between the capacity bound and the observation is `capacity_bytes - router_state_bytes` = 48,088 - 40,104 = 7,984 bytes, i.e. 0.68% of the 1,182,568-byte total, because the dominant term by far is `maximum_support_bytes` = 1,134,480 (95.9%) -- and that term is an observation on the ADRN side compared against an observation-that-equals-capacity on the comparator side. So the 'three different rules' produce a sub-1% distortion in a comparison whose two operands differ by 912 KB, and the harness additionally publishes `actual_online_state_bytes` (1,174,584) alongside so the bound component is fully separable.

killed_findings.refutation: Refuted directly by execution. `require_coverage` is an opt-in method with exactly one call site; it is not invoked by the constructor, by `StructuredBayesianRuleSearch.__init__`, or by `_evaluate_bayes_condition`. `DisclosedRuleGrammar.from_rules(splits.train + splits.validation)` constructs fine (I did it: size 24 at smoke, 80 at standard) and `_evaluate_bayes_condition(episodes=..., grammar=<ablated>, mode=...)` runs to completion and reports the numbers. killed_findings.refutation: The `context` argument is real (adrn2b_experiment.py:830-831, 845-846; keyed at adrn2b_bayes.py:724-732), but it is not a rule identifier. context_ids are minted from the SIGNATURE bank RNG -- `context_ids = tuple(f"ctx_{int(value):016x}" for value in raw_ids)` (adrn2b_tasks.py:494), seeded by `signature_seed` (adrn2b_tasks.py:838-844) -- and are then paired to rules by list position at line 851-854. killed_findings.dimension: train/validation/test hygiene of the meta-initializer and hyperparameter tuning
killed_findings.title: meta_initialization_scale is selected to maximise the exact curve integral whose points Gates C and E later report, on a validation arm configured identically to the test finalist
killed_findings.refutation: The described defect is not a defect. The finding concedes the episodes are disjoint, and that concession is fatal to it: selection runs on meta-validation episodes built from splits.validation (experiment.py:1263-1349), while every gate number is measured on meta-test episodes constructed afterwards from disjoint rules (1377-1397, disjointness enforced at 1207-1211). Choosing a hyperparameter on a validation split to maximize the metric you care about, then reporting that metric once on a disjoint test split, is the textbook-correct procedure -- and the test split IS the "held-out re-estimation" the finding says is absent. The winner's curse inflates the selected VALIDATION score, not the test estimate, which is conditionally unbiased given the selection; there is no test-set multiplicity because only the one frozen configuration is evaluated. Magnitude is negligible too: sweeping meta_initialization_scale over all four declared trials on the actual test episodes gives A(8) = 0.5464 / 0.5446 / 0.5471 / 0.5423 and A(32) = 0.5717 / 0.5753 / 0.5736 / 0.5756 -- a 0.005 spread, smaller than the paired bootstrap noise on those same statistics (CI half-widths ~0.005-0.016). The finding's own closing parenthetical is also wrong in the opposite direction: Gates A and D are affected by the selection, since the chosen learning rate, novelty threshold and meta scale all govern the context_visit > 1 records those gates read (my sweep moves the finalist's recall from 0.435 to 0.517 across the four scale trials).
